MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Low-grade intermediate grade osseous contusion involving the superior posterior lateral femoral condyle. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Mucoid degeneration without full-thickness disruption.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Low to intermediate grade osseous contusion involving the superior posterolateral femoral condyle.
2.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis, no tendon tear.

Clinical information: Left knee pain, refractory to opioids. Please assess for internal derangement.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the left knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
The cruciate ligaments are intact. There is mild thickening of the proximal medial collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. There is mild tendinosis of the distal quadriceps tendon. Otherwise extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There is a degenerative oblique tear at the posterior horn/posterior aspect body of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface (12-20). There are no unstable meniscal fragments. There is a mild mucoid degeneration of the lateral meniscus.

There is a mild chondrosis in the medial femorotibial joint compartment. There is a moderate chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment with a focal button osteophyte at the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle measuring 0.8 x 0.5 x 0.3 cm. There is no adjacent bone marrow edema. There is a moderate patellofemoral chondrosis with focal cartilage fibrillation and deep cartilage defects at the lateral patellar facet. The joint indications are well-maintained.

The infrapatellar fat pad is unremarkable. There is a mild joint effusion. There are no intra-articular bodies. 

There is a low volume Baker's cyst. There is a thickening with associated edematous changes involving the medial patellar plica (13-10)

The visualized muscle bulk is unremarkable. There is mild thickening with associated T2 hyperintensity of the proximal popliteal tendon in keeping with a mild tendinosis.

Conclusion:
1. Degenerative oblique tear posterior horn/posterior aspect body of the medial meniscus.
2. No acute ligamentous injury.
3. Moderate chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment with a small button osteophyte.
4. Moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
5. Thickening with associated edematous changes of the medial patellar plica. This may be seen in medial patellar plica syndrome. Please correlate clinically.
